1.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 26:3.

2.q: צַו֮ אֶת בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וְ⁠נָתְנ֣וּ לַ⁠לְוִיִּ֗ם מִֽ⁠נַּחֲלַ֛ת אֲחֻזָּתָ֖⁠ם עָרִ֣ים לָ⁠שָׁ֑בֶת
2.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as a direct quotation. Alternate translation: [Command the sons of Israel, ‘You shall give to the Levites from the inheritance of your possession cities to dwell in’]

2.q: וְ⁠נָתְנ֣וּ לַ⁠לְוִיִּ֗ם מִֽ⁠נַּחֲלַ֛ת אֲחֻזָּתָ֖⁠ם עָרִ֣ים לָ⁠שָׁ֑בֶת
2.note: The implication is that the Levites would not receive a territory of their own, as the other tribes would, so the other tribes needed to give them cities to live in. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and since the Levites will not receive a territory of their own, they shall give to the Levites from the inheritance of their possession cities to dwell in]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe an **inheritance** that is characterized by being the **possession** of the tribes of Israel. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [from the inheritance that they will possess]

The pronoun **you** refers to the Israelites, not to Moses. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. This also occurs in verses 4, 6, and 7. Alternate translation: [you Israelites shall give to the Levites]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:2. This also occurs in verses 8, 10, 15, and 34.

3.note: This could mean: (1) items that they would use for farming or tending animals. Alternate translation: [and for their farming equipment] (2) sheep and goats. Alternate translation: [and for their flock]

4.q: וּ⁠מִגְרְשֵׁי֙ הֶֽ⁠עָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּתְּנ֖וּ לַ⁠לְוִיִּ֑ם מִ⁠קִּ֤יר הָ⁠עִיר֙ וָ⁠ח֔וּצָ⁠ה אֶ֥לֶף אַמָּ֖ה סָבִֽיב & וּ⁠מַדֹּתֶ֞ם מִ⁠ח֣וּץ לָ⁠עִ֗יר אֶת־פְּאַת־קֵ֣דְמָ⁠ה אַלְפַּ֪יִם בָּֽ⁠אַמָּ֟ה וְ⁠אֶת־פְּאַת־נֶגֶב֩ אַלְפַּ֨יִם בָּ⁠אַמָּ֜ה וְ⁠אֶת־פְּאַת־יָ֣ם אַלְפַּ֣יִם בָּֽ⁠אַמָּ֗ה וְ⁠אֵ֨ת פְּאַ֥ת צָפ֛וֹן אַלְפַּ֥יִם בָּ⁠אַמָּ֖ה וְ⁠הָ⁠עִ֣יר בַּ⁠תָּ֑וֶךְ
4.note: This could mean: (1) that there was a block of land along each side of the city that was 1,000 cubits deep and 2,000 cubits long. Alternate translation: [And the pasturelands of the cities that you shall give to the Levites shall be 1,000 cubits, measured directly away from the wall of the city all around. And you shall measure the width of the land on each side: the edge to the east 2,000 by the cubit, and the edge of the south 2,000 by the cubit, and the edge of the west 2,000 by the cubit, and the edge of the north 2,000 by the cubit, and the city in the midst] (2) that the land on each side of the city was 1,000 cubits deep. Ignoring the size of the city itself, that would create a square that measured 2,000 cubits on each side. Alternate translation: [And the pasturelands of the cities that you shall give to the Levites shall be from the wall of the city and outside 1,000 cubits all around. So, you shall measure the total land outside the city: the edge to the east 2,000 by the cubit, and the edge of the south 2,000 by the cubit, and the edge of the west 2,000 by the cubit, and the edge of the north 2,000 by the cubit. Adjust the shape of this area to include the city in the middle] (3) that the city had sides that were 2,000 cubits long. So, when the land was measured from the center of the town, the edge of the land was 2,000 cubits away. When the land was measured from the edge of the town, the edge of the land was 1,000 cubits away. Alternate translation: [And the pasturelands of the cities that you shall give to the Levites shall be 1,000 cubits all around when you measure from the wall outward. When you measure from the center of the city to each edge: the edge to the east 2,000 by the cubit, and the edge of the south 2,000 by the cubit, and the edge of the west 2,000 by the cubit, and the edge of the north 2,000 by the cubit]

These **cubits** were a unit of measurement corresponding to the distance between an average person’s elbow and middle fingertip, or about 46 centimeters or 18 inches. So 1,000 cubits would be about 460 meters or 1,500 feet. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express this distance in modern measurements, either in the text or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [about 1,500 feet]

5.note: A **cubit** was a unit of measurement corresponding to the distance between an average person’s elbow and middle fingertip, or about 46 centimeters or 18 inches. So 2,000 cubits would be about 920 meters or 3,000 feet. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express this distance in modern measurements, either in the text or a footnote. The same distance is given for each of the other three sides in this verse. Alternate translation: [the edge to the east about 3,000 feet]

6.note: The implication is that **the one having killed** is someone who has killed another person and is fleeing to one of these cities to be safe from anyone who wants to kill him in revenge. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. This also occurs in verse 11. Alternate translation: [for the fleeing there of the one having killed another person, so that he may be safe from anyone seeking revenge]

7.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [you shall give them together with their pasturelands]

8.q: מֵ⁠אֵ֤ת הָ⁠רַב֙ תַּרְבּ֔וּ וּ⁠מֵ⁠אֵ֥ת הַ⁠מְעַ֖ט תַּמְעִ֑יטוּ
8.note: Yahweh is using the adjectives **many** and **few** as nouns to mean tribes that have much land and tribes that have little land. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate these adjectives with equivalent phrases. Alternate translation: [from with the tribes that have much land you shall increase, and from with the tribes that have little land you shall decrease]

Here the masculine term **man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [Each one]

Yahweh is using **according to the mouth of his inheritance** as a common expression of the culture to mean “in proportion to the size of the land that he inherits.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in proportion to the size of his inheritance]

9.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 18:25.

10.q: דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵ⁠הֶ֑ם
10.note: See how you translated this expression in 33:51.

11.note: Yahweh is using **make happen for you cities** as a common expression of the culture to mean “select cities for this purpose.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [then you shall designate cities for yourselves]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **mistake**, you could express the same idea in another way. This also occurs in verse 15. Alternate translation: [one having struck a person without meaning to]

12.note: The **one redeeming** is a kind of close relative who has the responsibility to avenge the death of a family member by killing the person who killed him. If your readers would not be familiar with what this is, you could use the name of a similar role that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [for refuge from the relative seeking revenge]
See how you translated this expression in 16:9.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **judgment**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [so that they may judge him]

14.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 34:15.

15.note: A **sojourner** is a kind of foreigner who lived among the Israelites for a long time, and a **temporary resident** is a kind of foreigner who stayed among them for a shorter time. If your readers would not be familiar with these kinds of people, you could use the names of similar kinds of people that your readers would recognize, or you could use more general terms. Alternate translation: [and for the long-term foreigner and for the short-term foreigner]

16.note: Yahweh is presenting a possible condition: that a person might strike someone with an object made of iron and cause that person to die. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. Alternate translation: [But suppose he struck him with a vessel of iron and he died]

16.q: בִּ⁠כְלִ֨י בַרְזֶ֧ל הִכָּ֛ה⁠וּ וַ⁠יָּמֹ֖ת רֹצֵ֣חַֽ ה֑וּא
16.note: The pronouns **he** and **him** refer to different people in this verse. The first **he** and the last **he** refer to the person who struck someone, while **him** and the second **he** refer to the person who was struck. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the attacker struck the other person with a vessel of iron and that person died, the attacker is one having killed]

The implication is that the word **vessel** refers here to any tool or object, not only to a container. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [with an object made of iron]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb translated as **Dying** and **put to death** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. This also occurs in verses 17, 18, 21, and 31. Alternate translation: [The one having killed must certainly be put to death]

The expression **shall be put to death** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to state who would do the action, the context indicates that it would be the close relative who avenges the dead person. This also occurs in verses 17, 18, 21, and 31. Alternate translation: [the avenger shall put the one having killed to death]

17.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **stone** that is characterized by being small enough to hold in a **hand**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [with a stone small enough to hold in his hand]

19.note: Here, **the blood** represents “the death of a relative whom someone killed.” The person **redeeming the blood** is the close relative who had the responsibility to avenge that death. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. This also occurs in verses 21, 24, 25, and 27. Alternate translation: [The one avenging the death of his relative]

Yahweh is using **In his meeting with him** as a common expression of the culture to mean “whenever he finds him.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. This also occurs in verse 21. Alternate translation: [As soon as he finds him]

21.note: The implication is that the person struck the other person with his bare **hand** without using any weapon, and yet he killed him intentionally. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [he struck him with just his fist, without using any weapon]

22.note: Yahweh uses the word **But** here to indicate a contrast between the cases in which a person kills someone on purpose, which the previous verses describe, and the cases in which a person kills someone by accident, which this verse and the next verse describe. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [On the other hand, if]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **suddenness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [unexpectedly]

23.q: א֣וֹ בְ⁠כָל אֶ֜בֶן אֲשֶׁר יָמ֥וּת בָּ⁠הּ֙ בְּ⁠לֹ֣א רְא֔וֹת
23.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [or if with any stone by which a person could die, while he did not see the other person]

24.note: Here the word “blood” is a metonym for the murder. See how you translated this phrase in Numbers 35:19. Alternate translation: [the one who avenges the murder] or [the relative seeking vengeance]

25.note: Here, **hand** represents “power” or “control.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from the power of the one redeeming the blood]

The implication is that the death of the **great priest**, that is, the high priest, would end the time that the person who killed someone had to stay in the city of refuge. After that, he could safely return home. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. This also occurs in verse 28. Alternate translation: [only until he may safely return home at the death of the high priest]

The pronoun **he** does not refer to the person who killed someone. It refers to an unspecified person who anointed the priest. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [whom another person anointed]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **oil** that is characterized by being set apart for use in **the holy place**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [with the oil that is set apart for use in the holy place]

26.note: Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb translated as **going out** and **goes out** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [But if the one having killed actually goes out]

27.note: Yahweh is using **there is not to him blood** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the one redeeming the blood is not guilty of murder.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he is not guilty of murder]

29.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 27:11.

30.q: כָּל מַ֨כֵּה נֶ֔פֶשׁ לְ⁠פִ֣י עֵדִ֔ים יִרְצַ֖ח אֶת הָ⁠רֹצֵ֑חַ
30.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **Everyone having struck a person** with the information about **the one having killed**, since both phrases refer to the same person. Alternate translation: [To the mouth of witnesses he shall kill everyone who has struck and killed a person]

Here, **mouth** represents “testimony,” what the witnesses say about what happened. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [on the testimony of witnesses]

The pronoun **he** does not refer to the person who killed someone. It refers to whoever carries out the execution, such as the close relative who avenges the dead person. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the one redeeming the blood shall kill the one having killed]

Yahweh is using **answer against a person** as a common expression of the culture to mean “testify against a person.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And one witness shall not testify against a person]

31.note: Yahweh is using **who is wicked to die** as a common expression of the culture to mean “who is guilty and deserves to die.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [who is guilty and deserves to be executed]

32.q: וְ⁠לֹא־תִקְח֣וּ כֹ֔פֶר לָ⁠נ֖וּס אֶל־עִ֣יר מִקְלָט֑⁠וֹ לָ⁠שׁוּב֙ לָ⁠שֶׁ֣בֶת בָּ⁠אָ֔רֶץ
32.note: The implication is that someone could offer a ransom payment in order to be allowed to leave the city of refuge before the death of the high priest. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And you shall not accept payment from someone in exchange for allowing him to leave the city of his refuge and return to live in his own land before the death of the priest]

33.q: כִּ֣י הַ⁠דָּ֔ם ה֥וּא יַחֲנִ֖יף אֶת הָ⁠אָ֑רֶץ
33.note: Here, **the blood** represents “the killing of a person.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [for murder pollutes the land]

33.q: וְ⁠לָ⁠אָ֣רֶץ לֹֽא יְכֻפַּ֗ר לַ⁠דָּם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שֻׁפַּךְ בָּ֔⁠הּ כִּי אִ֖ם בְּ⁠דַ֥ם שֹׁפְכֽ⁠וֹ
33.note: If it would appear in your language that Yahweh was making a statement and then contradicting it, you could reword this as a positive statement. Alternate translation: [and atonement for the land can be made for the blood that was poured out in it only by the blood of the one pouring it out]

The expression **shall not be made** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and you cannot make atonement for the land]

The expression **was poured out** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [for the blood that someone poured out in it]

Yahweh is using **the blood of the one pouring it out** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the death of the person who killed someone.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [by the death of the person who killed someone]

34.q: וְ⁠לֹ֧א תְטַמֵּ֣א אֶת־הָ⁠אָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתֶּם֙ יֹשְׁבִ֣ים בָּ֔⁠הּ
34.note: The word **you** in the phrase **you shall not make unclean** is singular here because Yahweh is speaking to each individual Israelite. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction. The word **you** in the phrase **you are dwelling** is plural because Yahweh is speaking to all the Israelites. So use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction

34.q: וְ⁠לֹ֧א תְטַמֵּ֣א אֶת הָ⁠אָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתֶּם֙ יֹשְׁבִ֣ים בָּ֔⁠הּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י שֹׁכֵ֣ן בְּ⁠תוֹכָ֑⁠הּ כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה שֹׁכֵ֕ן בְּ⁠ת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
34.note: The word translated as **for** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [And because I, Yahweh, am dwelling in the midst of the sons of Israel, you shall not make unclean the land in which you are dwelling, in the midst of which I am dwelling]
